cards.text: Amos, a sheepherder from Tekoa, has been bringing the LORD's judgment on nation after nation: Damascus, Gaza, Tyre, Edom, the Ammonites, Moab and even Judah (Amos 1:1-2:5). Now the LORD says that for three transgressions of Israel, even four, He will not revoke His judgment. I bet Israel was nodding along right up until they heard their OWN name.

cards.question: The LORD's first charge is that Israel sells the righteous for silver. What do they sell the needy for?

cards.text: Then the LORD says they trample on the heads of the poor as on the dust of the earth. Friend, I spent YEARS under the dust in the back of a junk drawer, and NOBODY should get treated like dust.

cards.question: Israel tramples on the heads of the poor. What do they do to the needy who are in their way?

answers.text: They push them out of the way
They mock them in the streets

cards.text: Then the LORD names something else they do. A man and his father have relations with the same girl.

cards.question: The LORD says what a man and his father do with the same girl profanes His holy name.

cards.text: And the LORD keeps going. In the house of their God, they drink wine obtained through fines.

cards.question: Israel also lies down beside every altar. What do they lie on?

cards.text: Then the LORD brings up the Amorite, the people in the land before Israel, tall like the cedars and as strong as the oaks. Friend, I'm a cookie stamper, and some days I LOSE a wrestling match with an oven mitt.

cards.question: Israel beat the Amorite because Israel's men were even taller and stronger.

cards.text: Not even close. The LORD says He destroyed the Amorite, fruit above and roots below, and He brought Israel up from the land of Egypt.

cards.question: After Egypt, the LORD led Israel ___ years in the wilderness, so they could take possession of the land of the Amorite.

cards.text: He also raised up prophets from their sons and Nazirites from their young men. Then the LORD asks, "Is this not true, O children of Israel?"

cards.question: Israel honors the prophets the LORD raised up and lets them prophesy.
And the Nazirites the LORD raised up? Israel made them drink ___.

cards.text: Ordering the prophets to stop prophesying is like yanking the battery out of the smoke detector because the beeping is getting on your nerves. Then the LORD says, "Behold, I am about to crush you in your place as with a cart full of grain."

cards.question: Israel has swift runners, strong men and mighty warriors. When the LORD crushes them, what will a strong man's strength do for him?
On that day, the archer, the fleet of foot and the horseman will at least get away.
What does the LORD say even the bravest of mighty men will do on that day?

findings.problem: The joke compares two different actions. Amos 2:7 is about being trampled like dust. Papa Dorin's drawer line is about lying under dust, forgotten. Those don't match, so the comparison doesn't click. The line also ends as a gentle moral instead of a laugh.

rule.text: The everyday comparison must have the same action.

findings.problem: The question says 'the needy who are in their way.' The right answer, 'They push them out of the way,' repeats that wording. It stands out from the other two answers, so the card tests wording instead of the moment.

rule.text: Don't let the right answer stand out. All the answers should sound alike. None should sound more like the Bible, or more modern, than the others.

findings.problem: The smoke detector comparison gives a reason Israel silenced the prophets: 'because the beeping is getting on your nerves.' Amos 2:12 gives no reason. It only says they commanded the prophets not to prophesy. The joke needs to keep the action (silencing a warning) without adding a motive.

rule.text: He never adds why someone did, said or thought something unless the text says why.

findings.problem: The right answer is the only negative ('It won't help him prevail'). Both wrong answers are positive. The setup ('When the LORD crushes them') makes the right answer easy to spot. Also, 'win' and 'prevail' mean the same thing, so the two answers differ only by 'won't.'

rule.text: Don't let the right answer stand out. All the answers should sound alike.

findings.problem: The statement covers the archer, the fleet of foot and the horseman. Amos 2:15 says the fleet of foot will not escape and the horseman will not save his life. For the archer, it only says he will not stand his ground. It says nothing about whether he gets away. 'False' is not clearly true for every group, so a baker could argue the point.

rule.text: A card about two groups needs an answer true for both. When a question covers more than one group, like the sea creatures and the birds, the right answer must be true for every group in it.
